newsitem.title: TANZANIA: 31 dead in Zanzibar cholera outbreak - report.
newsitem.headline: 31 dead in Zanzibar cholera outbreak - report.

text.p: At least 31 people have died and more than 260 others have been infected by a cholera outbreak on Zanzibar, Tanzania's semi-official Sunday News reported.

It said the cholera outbreak, first identified in March, had forced the Indian Ocean island government to order restaurants closed. Cholera cases -- believed to be spread by contaminated food or water -- have been reported from the main Zanzibar island and also from the nearby Pemba island.

Zanzibar joined mainland Tanganyika to form the United Republic of Tanzania after a revolution which overthrew the last Arab Sultan in 1964. But with its own parliament and president, Zanzibar retains a large measure of autonomy within Tanzania.
Senior western aid officials who asked not to be identified told Reuters the outbreak appeared to be a serious one.
The Sunday News quoted senior Zanzibar tourism officials as saying the cholera outbreak had hit the tourism sector, one of Zanzibar's main sources of income.
Zanzibar Tourism Commission executive secretary Walid Fikirini said charter flights bringing up to 2,000 Italian tourists per week had been suspended, the newspaper added.
